CameraVideoThread

class CameraVideoThread(camera_index, use_low_resolution=False)[source]

Bases: QThread, QObject

Capture, analyze and annotate camera frames in a thread.

Parameters:
camera_indexint

OpenCV index of the camera.

use_low_resolutionbool, optional

If True, set the width and height configured in CalibrationService on the camera. Default is False.

Attributes:
change_pixmap_signalSignal(QImage)

Emitted for each processed frame with an RGB888 copy of the annotated image.

error_signalSignal(str)

Emitted with a translated message when the camera cannot be opened or a frame cannot be read.

camera_indexint

OpenCV index of the camera.

runningbool

Loop flag; True on creation, set to False by stop.

mp_managerMediaPipeManager

Pose detector.

use_low_resolutionbool

Whether the configured resolution is applied.

filterMediaPipeFilter

Frame enhancement and landmark smoothing.

serviceCalibrationService

Source of the camera, filter, pose and telemetry settings.

last_timestamp_msint

Timestamp of the last frame sent to MediaPipe.

Notes

The configured resolution is applied only when use_low_resolution is True, the opposite of CameraVideo. TODO(doc): is this inversion intended?

User-facing texts (error messages and telemetry labels) use self.tr() (runtime Qt translation).

Methods

put_text_unicode

Draw Unicode text on an OpenCV image using PIL.

run

Capture and process frames until stopped or the camera fails.

Stop the capture loop and wait for the thread to finish.
run()[source]

Capture and process frames until stopped or the camera fails.

Runs in the thread when start() is called.

Notes

For each frame:

  1. The mean brightness (V channel in HSV) is measured.

  2. MediaPipeFilter.apply_enhancements runs if is_filter_enable_filter().

  3. If is_enable_mediapipe_pose(), the pose is detected and smoothed, and the skeleton is drawn (green landmarks, red connections). Timestamps are forced to increase by at least 1 ms, as MediaPipe VIDEO mode requires.

  4. If is_telemetry_enable_panel(), the panel shows FPS (green at 15 or more, red below), brightness and the feet tracking confidence: the mean visibility of landmarks 31 and 32, green above 0.5, red otherwise. The confidence is shown as a 0-1 value although the label says “%”.

  5. The frame is emitted through change_pixmap_signal.

When a frame cannot be read, error_signal is emitted and the loop ends. The camera is released on exit.

stop()[source]

Stop the capture loop and wait for the thread to finish.

put_text_unicode(img, text, position, font_size=20, color=(255, 255, 255), font_path=None)[source]

Draw Unicode text on an OpenCV image using PIL.

OpenCV’s putText cannot render accented characters, so the image is converted to PIL, drawn and converted back.

Parameters:
imgnumpy.ndarray

BGR image from OpenCV.

textstr

Text to draw.

positiontuple[int, int]

(x, y) of the top-left corner of the text.

font_sizeint, optional

Font size in points. Default is 20.

colortuple[int, int, int], optional

Text color in BGR. Default is white.

font_pathstr | None, optional

TrueType font file. Default is None, which tries DejaVuSans.ttf (Linux), then arial.ttf (Windows), then PIL’s default font.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

New BGR image with the text drawn.
